title: They assumed nothing would follow, so they stopped seeing.
subtitle: How feeling safe from consequences dulls the heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains that they {trap}thought there would be no trial or repercussion{/trap} for the wrongs they did, so they became blind and deaf to the truth. Then {reward}Allah turned to them in forgiveness{/reward}, and many of them went back to the same blindness. The verse ends: Allah sees what they do.
now: The first time you skipped a prayer, it felt heavy. Nothing happened. The second time, lighter. A year later you do not notice anymore. That quiet slide is {trap}the eyes closing slowly{/trap}. And the mercy is that the door reopens, again and again. {idea}Walk through it and keep your eyes open this time.{/idea}
old: Nothing bad happened, so it must not matter much.
new: Getting away with something can be the very thing that blinds me.
try: Name one wrong you have stopped feeling bad about. Ask Allah to make you feel it again.

title: The Messiah himself said: worship Allah, my Lord and yours.
subtitle: A messenger pointing away from himself
then: Ibn Kathir notes that the first words of 'Isa, even as a baby in the cradle, were {idea}I am a servant of Allah.{/idea} As a grown prophet he told the Children of Israel: {idea}worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.{/idea} The verse then states soberly that {trap}setting up partners with Allah closes Paradise{/trap}, and the wrongdoers have no helpers.
now: A good teacher, a beloved sheikh, a parent you admire. Real love can slide into something else: you check what they would say before you check what Allah said. The best of them would say what the Messiah said: {idea}worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.{/idea} Honour them by following where they point.
old: The closer I feel to a righteous person, the closer I am to Allah.
new: The righteous point away from themselves, toward Allah alone.
try: Think of someone whose words you treat as final. Today, look up what Allah says on one thing they taught.

title: There is no god except One God.
subtitle: The line the whole surah keeps returning to
then: The verse answers a belief that made Allah one of three. As-Suddi linked it to {trap}taking 'Isa and his mother as gods beside Allah{/trap}, as the end of this surah also describes. The reply is short: {idea}there is no god but One God.{/idea} The warning is tied to a condition: if they do not stop.
now: Your heart can split its trust three ways without saying a word: Allah, your salary, and your own cleverness. When the job wobbles, everything wobbles. {idea}One God{/idea} means one place your heart finally rests. Everything else is a gift from Him, {trap}not a second pillar beside Him.{/trap}
old: I trust Allah, plus my income, plus my plans, equally.
new: Only One is God. My plans and income are tools He gave me.
try: Before checking your bank app today, say: my provision is from Allah alone.

title: Even then: will they not turn back to Him?
subtitle: An invitation after the gravest claim
then: Right after the heaviest warning, the very next verse asks a gentle question: {idea}will they not repent and seek His forgiveness?{/idea} Ibn Kathir calls this a sign of {reward}Allah's generosity, kindness and mercy{/reward}: even after so grave a claim, He calls them to return so He can forgive.
now: You have written someone off. A relative who did something unforgivable, a friend who wandered far. Or you have written yourself off. The Quran, straight after its sternest words, {reward}asks the door-question{/reward}. If Allah keeps the invitation open, {idea}you can stop closing it in your head.{/idea}
old: Some people, maybe me, are simply too far gone.
new: Allah calls even the gravest wrongdoers back. No one is outside the invitation.
try: Make one dua today for a person you had quietly given up on.

title: They both ate food.
subtitle: Honoured servants, not gods
then: The verse gives a calm, simple proof. 'Isa was {idea}a messenger like many before him{/idea}. His mother was a siddiqah, a woman of complete truthful faith. Ibn Kathir explains the point of {idea}they both used to eat food{/idea}: they needed nourishment like every servant of Allah, so they were servants, not gods.
now: Hunger at 4pm in Ramadan. You feel how much you need: water, food, sleep, air. That need is not a weakness to hide. {idea}It is the plain mark of being created.{/idea} The greatest people who ever lived carried that same mark, and it made them honoured servants, {trap}not less.{/trap}
old: Truly great people must be somehow beyond ordinary needs.
new: Even the greatest of people needed food. Needing is what servants do, and only Allah needs nothing.
try: At your next meal, pause before the first bite and thank Allah for meeting a need you cannot meet alone.

title: Why turn to what cannot help or harm you?
subtitle: The One who hears and knows
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask a direct question. Ibn Kathir explains it: how can anyone worship things that {trap}cannot prevent harm or bring benefit{/trap}, that do not hear, see or know, {idea}instead of Allah, who hears what His servants say and knows all things?{/idea}
now: The lucky charm in the car. The horoscope app you open "just for fun" before an interview. The person whose approval you check like a weather report. None of them {trap}heard you this morning{/trap}. {idea}Allah heard every word, even the ones you did not say.{/idea}
old: A little extra luck or reassurance on the side cannot hurt.
new: Only Allah hears me and can help me. Everything else hears nothing.
try: Remove one thing you keep for luck or reassurance, and ask Allah directly instead.

title: Do not go past the truth in your religion.
subtitle: Exaggeration, even in love, leads astray
then: Ibn Kathir explains the warning as: {trap}do not exaggerate in praising the one you were told to honour.{/trap} They raised a prophet to the rank of a god, because they followed teachers before them who {trap}went astray and misled many{/trap}. The fix is to stay {idea}within the truth{/idea}.
now: The online preacher you follow, whose every clip you share without checking. The relative who makes the religion so strict that the young people in the family quietly leave. Both {trap}add to the truth out of zeal{/trap}. {idea}Love for the deen means keeping it the size Allah made it.{/idea}
old: Going further than required can only be a good thing.
new: Going past the truth, even out of love, is still leaving the truth.
try: Before you share a religious clip today, check what the source is and whether it adds to what is known.

title: Their own prophets named the problem: constant disobedience.
subtitle: Why a curse came through Dawud and 'Isa
then: Allah says that those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed {idea}on the tongue of their own prophets, Dawud and 'Isa{/idea}. The verse states the reason clearly: {trap}they disobeyed and kept transgressing.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: disobeying Allah and wronging His creatures.
now: You hear a warning and think of other people. But the reason given is a behaviour, and behaviours travel. {trap}The small disobedience you repeat every day{/trap} is the same seed. The verse is a mirror: {idea}what you keep doing is what defines you.{/idea}
old: Warnings like this are about other people, not me.
new: The reason was a habit of disobedience, and that can grow in anyone, including me.
try: Pick one small sin you repeat daily. Skip it just for today.

title: No one told anyone to stop.
subtitle: A community where wrong goes unchallenged
then: Their habit was that {trap}they did not forbid one another from the wrong they did.{/trap} Ibn Kathir quotes the Prophet ﷺ: whoever sees a wrong should {idea}change it with his hand, then his tongue, then at least his heart{/idea}. He also quotes: fear of people should not stop you saying the truth you know, and that no one is asked to take on trials beyond what they can bear.
now: Your office jokes about a colleague who is not in the room. Everyone laughs a little. You can change the subject, say "not cool", or at least not laugh. {idea}Each of those counts.{/idea} The only option that does not is {trap}joining in because everyone else is.{/trap}
old: Speaking up is someone else's job, I would only make it awkward.
new: There is always some level I can act at, even if it is only in my heart.
try: Next time a cruel joke starts, change the subject or simply do not laugh.

title: What you send ahead by the side you take.
subtitle: Loyalty given to those who oppose the truth
then: Mujahid said this verse refers to the hypocrites. Ibn Kathir explains that by {trap}giving their loyalty to those who rejected faith instead of the believers{/trap}, they sent ahead an evil deed for themselves. It planted hypocrisy in their hearts and {trap}brought Allah's anger.{/trap}
now: At work there is a crowd that mocks anything to do with faith. To fit in, you laugh along, hide your prayer, roll your eyes when they do. Then you start {trap}defending them against the people who care about you{/trap}. Whose side you take is {idea}something you are sending ahead of yourself.{/idea}
old: Who I side with socially is just a matter of convenience.
new: The side I take is a deed I send ahead, and it shapes my heart.
try: Do one small thing today that shows openly which values you stand with, kindly.

title: Real faith would have chosen different friends.
subtitle: Belief shows in whom you lean on
then: The verse explains the root. Ibn Kathir: {idea}had they sincerely believed in Allah, His Messenger and the Quran{/idea}, they would not have secretly supported those against the believers. But {trap}many of them were defiant{/trap}. Their friendships exposed what their words hid.
now: Scroll through the five people you message most. The ones whose opinions you repeat. The ones you go to when things fall apart. {idea}That list says something about your faith{/idea} that a status update cannot. It is never too late to {reward}add someone good to it.{/reward}
old: My faith is between me and Allah, my friends are a separate matter.
new: The people I lean on reveal what I truly believe.
try: Message one person who helps you be better and arrange to see them this week.
